title: Lawmakers prepare bill requiring AI ‘kill switch’
slides: Who will control AI when it turns dangerous?
Lawmakers now propose a mandatory kill switch.
But this switch could also be exploited by hackers.
Your AI investments may face new compliance costs.
Audit your AI systems for emergency shutdown readiness.
thread_text:
1. Who holds the kill switch?

Lawmakers want a mandatory shutdown button in every AI system. But that button is a new attack surface.

2. Hackers love a single point of failure.

A kill switch is a backdoor by design. If it's in every system, one exploit can freeze them all.

3. Compliance isn't optional anymore.

Regulators will demand proof of emergency shutdown readiness. Your AI budget just got a new line item.

4. Audit for the worst case.

Test your AI's kill switch now. A simulated failure could save you from a real one.

5. Run a shutdown drill this week.

Pick one AI tool you use daily. Try to kill it remotely. If you can't, you're not ready.

instagram.caption:
Lawmakers are drafting a bill that would force every AI system to include a mandatory kill switch. 🛑

That off switch is meant to shut down dangerous AI. But it's also a built-in backdoor — hackers could exploit a single vulnerability to freeze every system at once. 🔐

If you build or use AI tools, you'll soon need to prove emergency shutdown readiness. Compliance costs just hit your budget.

What happens when the kill switch becomes the target? Run one shutdown drill on a tool you use daily — can you kill it remotely?
